purpose: Maps the 44 roadmap skills extracted from the user's two roadmap sites onto the competency framework, records what each skill still needs before lessons can be written, and carries the audit findings that resulted from comparing the roadmaps with current published descriptions of AI-engineering work.
status_semantics: See knowledge/states.json. The status recorded here is the status of the *topic*, not of any lesson.
prerequisites_note: Skill-level prerequisites are recorded only where the dependency is concrete. Where a skill depends on a competency rather than on another skill of the roadmap, the competency is named in `requires_competencies`.

skills.name: Python Programming
skills.source_need: The user's nominated book (Python Crash Course) and one of the two nominated courses; currently no programming source is in the repository.
skills.audit_note: Split across three competencies because writing idiomatic Python, handling errors, and using functional tooling are separately assessable and are taught at different points.

skills.name: SQL
skills.source_need: The nominated SQL book and a practice environment with real datasets.
skills.audit_note: The roadmap allocates 10 days, which is reasonable for a working level; the audit keeps the target at `applied` because window functions and query planning are what production work uses.

skills.name: Linear Algebra
skills.source_need: Supplied: chapters 2-4 of Mathematics for Machine Learning. Still needed: a numerical-linear-algebra source for MATH-19, and a vectorised-computing source for CS-03.
skills.audit_note: The roadmap's own day plan allots one day to 'SVD & PCA' and one to 'ML applications' (days 30-31). The supplied book devotes two chapters to matrix decompositions, and the target level for these competencies is `deep`. The proposal is to keep the seven days as a first pass and to let the lesson modules define the real depth, rather than compressing the material to fit the schedule.

skills.name: Probability & Statistics
skills.source_need: Supplied: chapter 6 of Mathematics for Machine Learning, with estimation material in chapters 8-9. Still needed: a statistics source that covers hypothesis testing, confidence intervals and applied statistical reasoning, which the supplied book does not teach.
skills.audit_note: The roadmap names 'Naked Statistics' as the book, which the audit records as a mismatch: it builds intuition but does not support the estimation and Gaussian material the later roadmap skills depend on. The supplied book is the stronger source for this skill; the recommendation is to use both, with clearly separated roles.

skills.name: Git & Version Control
skills.source_need: The nominated free Git reference and the interactive branching tutorial.
skills.audit_note: Adds CAREER-02 because reviewing changes is part of the same workflow and is not otherwise covered.

skills.name: Linux / Command Line
skills.source_need: A shell and Linux source matching the shell in use.
skills.audit_note: Merged with environment and packaging management, since the roadmap's own 'virtual environments, package management' content in SK-01 is the same competency.

skills.name: Data Structures
skills.source_need: A data-structures source plus a practice schedule.
skills.audit_note: Classified as `recommended` rather than `essential` for the engineering work itself, and `essential` for interview preparation. The distinction is recorded so that time spent here is a deliberate choice.

skills.name: Algorithms & Big-O
skills.source_need: An algorithms source plus a practice schedule.
skills.audit_note: 22 combined days for SK-07 and SK-08 is the largest foundation block in the plan. Justified for interview readiness; for engineering work the more valuable adjacent competency is CS-03, which the roadmap does not name as a skill.

skills.name: Design Patterns & SOLID
skills.source_need: A design source written for Python rather than for Java.
skills.audit_note: Narrowed deliberately: patterns are taught as answers to specific maintainability problems, not as a catalogue to memorise.

skills.name: Web Frameworks (FastAPI / Django)
skills.source_need: Framework documentation current at the time of teaching.
skills.audit_note: Adds an explicit dependency on testing, because a service without tests is not a service. The roadmap currently places testing (SK-11) after this skill.

skills.name: Testing & TDD
skills.source_need: A pytest-centred testing source.
skills.audit_note: Sequencing defect: the timetable's Foundation Project Sprint (days 68-70, week 12) requires unit tests, but testing is scheduled in week 15. Either testing moves earlier or the sprint changes; the audit recommends moving testing into the foundation phase.

skills.name: Docker & Kubernetes
skills.source_need: Container documentation and a local-cluster exercise.
skills.audit_note: Overlaps SK-44. Proposed split: this skill teaches containers and basic orchestration; SK-44 is restricted to operational concerns (rollouts, scaling, resource policy) and is marked role-specific.

skills.name: CI/CD Pipelines
skills.source_need: Pipeline documentation plus a worked pipeline.
skills.audit_note: Adds a dependency on testing: continuous integration is the automated execution of checks that must exist first.

skills.name: Security (OWASP / Auth)
skills.source_need: OWASP material, authentication documentation, and AI-specific threat guidance.
skills.audit_note: Extended to cover the AI-specific threats (prompt injection, data exfiltration through tools) because neither roadmap names them and they are specific to the systems this curriculum targets.

skills.name: Async Programming
skills.source_need: Concurrency material for the Python version in use.
skills.audit_note: Target level is `working`, not `applied`: most AI-engineering code needs correct use of existing concurrency utilities rather than original concurrency design.

skills.name: System Design
skills.source_need: System-design material plus AI-specific case studies, which will be authored as original scenarios with rubrics.
skills.audit_note: Adds a dependency on the lifecycle competency, because an AI system design that omits evaluation and monitoring is incomplete rather than merely simplified.

skills.name: Apache Spark / PySpark
skills.source_need: Spark documentation and a dataset large enough to show partitioning effects.
skills.audit_note: Adds a dependency on pipeline design: the distributed engine executes a pipeline whose correctness was already decided.

skills.name: Apache Kafka
skills.source_need: Kafka documentation and an event-time exercise.
skills.audit_note: The competency is deliberately about event time, state and delivery semantics rather than about one product's API, so that a lesson remains useful if the tooling changes.

skills.name: Data Warehouses
skills.source_need: Warehouse documentation plus modelling material.
skills.audit_note: Paired with dimensional modelling rather than only with product documentation, because warehouse choice is downstream of the model.

skills.name: ETL / ELT Pipelines
skills.source_need: An ELT source plus orchestration tooling.
skills.audit_note: Adds a dependency on data quality, since validation is part of the pipeline rather than a later stage. The roadmap places data quality (SK-25) after this skill.

skills.name: Apache Airflow
skills.source_need: Airflow documentation and a backfill exercise.
skills.audit_note: Kept as its own skill because scheduling has its own failure modes (silent stalls, backfills, retries) that pipeline design does not cover.

skills.name: dbt
skills.source_need: dbt documentation and a modelling exercise.
skills.audit_note: Shares a competency with SK-20. The two skills are different tools for one competency, which is a deliberate overlap in the roadmap rather than a defect; the coverage report should not count them as independent coverage.

skills.name: Dimensional Modeling
skills.source_need: A dimensional-modelling source.
skills.audit_note: Target level `working`: engineers need to model a process correctly and to recognise the grain of a fact table, which is a design skill rather than a research skill.

skills.name: NoSQL Databases
skills.source_need: Storage-engine material covering the main families.
skills.audit_note: Reduced to `awareness` level, because the decision an engineer actually makes is which family to use and why, not how to build one.

skills.name: Data Quality & Testing
skills.source_need: Validation tooling plus drift-detection methods.
skills.audit_note: The supplied book contributes conceptually (Section 8.1 links data to generalisation) and is recorded as partial coverage rather than as a source for the tooling.

skills.name: Cloud Platforms (AWS / GCP / Azure)
skills.source_need: Official documentation for one provider, dated, plus a cost exercise.
skills.audit_note: The roadmap lists three providers in one skill. The competency is deliberately provider-agnostic so lessons can be written for whichever account the user has; claiming depth in three clouds from eight days would be dishonest.

skills.name: Classical Machine Learning
skills.source_need: Supplied: chapters 8-12 of Mathematics for Machine Learning, which cover empirical risk, estimation, linear regression, PCA, mixture models and SVM. Still needed: tree ensembles and the applied comparison of methods, which the supplied book does not cover.
skills.audit_note: The supplied book is strong here but narrow: two model families in depth plus the estimation theory that unifies them. The audit flags 'no gradient boosting, no trees, no applied model selection' as the main gap inside a topic the roadmap allocates 10 days.

skills.name: Deep Learning Fundamentals
skills.source_need: Supplied: Section 5.6 of Mathematics for Machine Learning for the mathematics of backpropagation and gradients in a deep network. Still needed: a deep-learning text for architectures, activations, training practice and regularisation, plus a framework source.
skills.audit_note: Coverage is partial and the audit says so: the supplied book teaches the calculus behind training a network, not deep learning as a field. A deep-learning source is required before these lessons can be written.

skills.name: PyTorch
skills.source_need: Framework documentation for the version in use, plus exercises.
skills.audit_note: Lessons for this skill must record the framework version they were checked against; framework behaviour in this area changes between releases.

skills.name: CNNs & Computer Vision
skills.source_need: A computer-vision source and a dataset.
skills.audit_note: Classified role-specific. Neither roadmap justifies vision for the user's stated goal beyond listing it, so it is recorded as recommended-if-vision-roles-are-targeted rather than essential.

skills.name: Transformers & NLP
skills.source_need: Primary references for attention and the transformer, plus a current architectural walkthrough, both dated.
skills.audit_note: Essential. Overlaps SK-37 (LLMs and fine-tuning) and SK-38 (RAG); the audit keeps the boundary at 'how the architecture works' here and 'how to adapt and use it' there.

skills.name: Model Evaluation & Metrics
skills.source_need: Supplied: Section 8.6 (nested cross-validation, Bayesian model selection) and Section 8.2 (expected risk) support ML-04. Still needed: metric selection, calibration and evaluation of free-form generative output.
skills.audit_note: The roadmap allocates four days to this skill. Published role analyses emphasise evaluation and data pipelines among what postings screen for [REF-002, REF-006], and generative evaluation is a competency of its own. The audit recommends treating evaluation as a larger block than the roadmap's four days suggest.

skills.name: Feature Engineering
skills.source_need: Supplied: partial, through the polynomial feature expansion used to demonstrate overfitting in Section 9.2. Still needed: a practical feature-engineering source covering categorical, temporal and text features.
skills.audit_note: The supplied book is used here for a principle (feature expansion changes model capacity), not for a catalogue of transformations.

skills.name: Experiment Tracking (MLflow / W&B)
skills.source_need: Tooling documentation and a reproducibility exercise.
skills.audit_note: Three days is short for a skill whose value depends on habit. The audit accepts the day count but recommends the exercise be embedded in every later modelling lesson rather than confined to this block.

skills.name: HuggingFace Ecosystem
skills.source_need: Library documentation for the version in use.
skills.audit_note: The roadmap treats a library ecosystem as a skill. The audit keeps it, but maps it onto competencies rather than treating fluency with one vendor's libraries as knowledge in itself.

skills.name: MLOps & Model Deployment
skills.source_need: MLOps principles from a primary source, serving-framework documentation, and a measurement exercise.
skills.audit_note: The audit treats production engineering as the largest gap between the roadmaps as written and what current role descriptions emphasise: the two roadmaps give it one named skill (8 days) plus observability. Splitting it into three competencies here is a proposal, not an existing roadmap topic.

skills.name: LLMs & Fine-Tuning (LoRA / RLHF)
skills.source_need: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning literature, framework documentation and model cards, all dated and version-recorded.
skills.audit_note: Essential and fast-moving. Every numerical claim (cost, memory, quality change) in a lesson for this skill must be dated and, where possible, measured in this environment rather than quoted.

skills.name: RAG & Vector Databases
skills.source_need: Vector-search and embedding documentation, retrieval evaluation methods, and a corpus to work on.
skills.audit_note: Extended from three to four competencies: the roadmap's seven days cover building a pipeline but not the retrieval evaluation or the cost/latency accounting that decide whether the pipeline is usable.

skills.name: Distributed Training
skills.source_need: Distributed-training documentation and a memory-accounting exercise.
skills.audit_note: Classified role-specific with an initial target of `awareness`. Most AI-engineering roles consume distributed training rather than implement it; the audit does not recommend deepening this until a target role requires it.

skills.name: Distributed Systems (Advanced)
skills.source_need: A distributed-systems source and incident case studies.
skills.audit_note: Overlaps SK-16 and SK-41. The audit proposes the boundary: SK-16 designs a system, this skill reasons about its failure and consistency behaviour, SK-41 is the streaming instance of the same questions.

skills.name: Streaming Systems (Flink / Spark Streaming)
skills.source_need: Stream-processing documentation.
skills.audit_note: Shares a competency with SK-18; two tools, one set of concepts. The coverage report counts the competency once.

skills.name: Data Lakehouse (Iceberg / Delta Lake)
skills.source_need: Table-format documentation for the version in use.
skills.audit_note: Marked `awareness`. Very version-sensitive; lessons must state the format version and the date of the last check.

skills.name: Observability & Monitoring
skills.source_need: Observability tooling documentation, drift-detection methods, and incident-review practice.
skills.audit_note: The audit adds incident response and cost visibility here, because the roadmap's five days cover dashboards and alerts but not what happens when they fire.

skills.name: Kubernetes Advanced / Helm
skills.source_need: Kubernetes and packaging documentation, with a local cluster.
skills.audit_note: Classified role-specific. If the target roles are application-layer AI engineering, the audit recommends not spending seven days here before PROD-01 through PROD-04 are covered.

audit_findings.finding: Production and operational competencies are underrepresented relative to what current role descriptions emphasise.
audit_findings.evidence: The two roadmaps give production ML one named skill (SK-36, 8 days) and monitoring one (SK-43, 5 days), out of 339 days. Published role analyses put deployment, monitoring, data pipelines and production engineering among the most-screened requirements, and place research methods in a small minority of postings [REF-002, REF-006].
audit_findings.recommendation: Promote production competencies (PROD-01 to PROD-07) to a first-class part of the path rather than a late specialisation phase, and add the four competencies the roadmaps do not name: incident response (PROD-04), cost and performance (PROD-06), AI security and privacy (PROD-05), responsible AI (PROD-07).

audit_findings.finding: A sequencing defect exists in the timetable: a required tool is used before it is taught.
audit_findings.evidence: The Foundation Project Sprint (days 68-70, week 12) instructs the learner to add 'unit tests (pytest)', while Testing and TDD (SK-11) is scheduled in week 15 as part of SWE Core.
audit_findings.recommendation: Move testing into the foundation phase, before the first sprint, or remove the test requirement from the sprint. The audit recommends the former: tests are needed to assess every later project.

audit_findings.finding: Mathematical foundations are allocated less time than the depth targets imply, and the deep target is not achievable inside the roadmap's day budget at the stated level.
audit_findings.evidence: SK-03 (7 days, 56 hours) covers vector spaces, linear mappings, determinants, eigendecomposition and the SVD; the supplied book devotes three chapters and about 120 pages to this material, and the extracted exercise sets contribute 41 items. The roadmap's own plan assigns one day to SVD and PCA combined (day 30).
audit_findings.recommendation: Keep the seven days as an orientation pass and let the lesson modules carry the depth, with an explicit note that the target level for MATH competencies is reached over repeated passes rather than within the scheduled block. Do not silently reduce the target level to match the schedule.

audit_findings.finding: The roadmap's nominated source for Probability & Statistics does not support the later skills that depend on it.
audit_findings.evidence: SK-04 names 'Naked Statistics' (an intuition-building book without calculus) while SK-27, SK-32 and SK-37 depend on estimation, distributions and uncertainty. The supplied book covers those topics formally (chapters 6, 8, 9) and is already in the repository.
audit_findings.recommendation: Use the supplied book as the primary source for the probabilistic competencies and keep the nominated book as motivational reading. Record both roles in the skill's source notes.

audit_findings.finding: Competencies absent from both roadmaps that current practice treats as part of the role.
audit_findings.evidence: Neither roadmap names: evaluation of generative output (GEN-04), prompting and context engineering (GEN-02), cost and latency engineering (GEN-06), AI security and privacy (PROD-05), responsible AI (PROD-07), or any professional-practice competency (CAREER-01 to CAREER-05). Generative evaluation and safety guidance now appear in role descriptions and platform documentation [REF-002, REF-007].
audit_findings.recommendation: Add GEN-02, GEN-04, GEN-06, PROD-05 and PROD-07 to the curriculum map (done here), and add CAREER-01 to CAREER-05 so that interview preparation and portfolio work have assessable criteria rather than only scheduled days.

audit_findings.finding: Several skills map onto the same competency, so the 44-skill count overstates the number of distinct things to learn.
audit_findings.evidence: SK-20 and SK-22 both map to DATA-03; SK-18 and SK-41 both map to DATA-06; SK-12 and SK-44 overlap on SWE-07; SK-27, SK-32 and SK-33 share ML-03/ML-04/ML-05 coverage. The roadmap's own description of SK-02 to SK-44 covers 44 named skills but 85 competencies and 10 domains.
audit_findings.recommendation: Keep the skills as the user's own plan and as navigation, but drive coverage and progress from competencies, so that two tools serving one competency are not counted as two independent accomplishments.

audit_findings.finding: Data-quality defects exist inside the two roadmap pages themselves and must not be propagated into the platform.
audit_findings.evidence: The timetable header states 2,720 total hours while its own stat row states 2,712; the resource index's filter legend states 'SWE (10), Data Eng (10), AI/ML (10), Specialization (6)' while its content contains 8, 8, 10, 10 and 8 skills; SK-01 declares 14 study days while its day plan numbers 13; several skill names differ between the two pages (for example SK-19 and SK-23). Full list: knowledge/roadmaps/data-quality-report.json.
audit_findings.recommendation: Treat page content as canonical, surface the discrepancies where the original pages are preserved, and derive every count shown in the new interface from the data model rather than from hand-written text.

audit_findings.finding: The timetable's day-level plan exists for only part of the curriculum.
audit_findings.evidence: The timetable contains detailed day-by-day blocks for skills 01-16 plus two project sprints (116 scheduled day entries); the remaining 28 skills exist only as sidebar entries with day counts. Total: 339 study days across 44 skills and 2 sprints.
audit_findings.recommendation: Record `plan_depth` per skill (already done in the extracted inventory) and never present a summary-only skill as if it had a detailed plan. The platform's learning-path view should show which skills have detailed sequences and which do not.

audit_findings.finding: The supplied book's exercise sets cannot be used as-is for assessment.
audit_findings.evidence: Chapters 2-7 supply 69 exercise items (verified against the PDF) with no solutions in the draft. Six of those items are mangled in the extraction and must be checked against the PDF before use. Chapters 8-12 supply no exercise sets at all.
audit_findings.recommendation: Use the source's items as exercise statements, clearly attributed, with our own worked solutions that are verified independently and labelled as ours rather than as the authors'. Author original exercises for chapters 8-12 and label them as original.

audit_findings.finding: The roadmap's per-day allocations assume a pace that should be treated as a plan rather than a constraint.
audit_findings.evidence: 339 study days at 8 hours is 2,712 hours over about 57 weeks at six days per week. Several skills with deep target levels carry three to five days (for example SK-34 Experiment Tracking at 3 days, SK-32 Model Evaluation at 4 days).
audit_findings.recommendation: Keep the schedule as the learner's plan, but let the curriculum model express effort separately from depth so that the interface never implies that a deep competency was completed in three days.

reconciliation.rule: Skill <-> competency links are unioned in both directions; see the same note in section-concept-map.json.
